pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Make use of indexed write GMBUS feature This patch enables the indexed write feature of the GMBUS to concatenate 2 consecutive messages into one. The criteria for an indexed write is that both messages are writes, the first is length == 1, and the second is length > 0. The first message is sent out by the GMBUS as the slave command, and the second one is sent via the GMBUS FIFO as usual. Changes in v3: - Added to series Changes in v4: - Combine indexed reads and writes (Ville) Changes in v5: - checkpatch whitespace nits Changes in v6: - None Reviewed-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Suggested-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180108195545.218615-7-seanpaul@chromium.org BUG=b:141971239 TEST=boot Meep, run login_LoginSuccess Signed-off-by: Chiou, Cooper <cooper.chiou@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit d02cf0a4f4db3bdbf1f7fa6915db0a96bd98ed9e) Change-Id: I13852b5d9309025239f92ecfec1f13c608c99301 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1857841 Tested-by: Cooper Chiou <cooper.chiou@intel.com> Commit-Ready: Marco Chen <marcochen@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Add function to output Aksv over GMBUS Once the Aksv is available in the PCH, we need to get it on the wire to the receiver via DDC. The hardware doesn't allow us to read the value directly, so we need to tell GMBUS to source the Aksv internally and send it to the right offset on the receiver. The way we do this is to initiate an indexed write where the index is the Aksv register offset. We write dummy values to GMBUS3 as if we were sending the key, and the hardware slips in the "real" values when it goes out. Changes in v2: - None Changes in v3: - Uses new index write feature (Ville) Changes in v4: - None Changes in v5: - checkpatch whitespace fix Changes in v6: - None Cc: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180108195545.218615-8-seanpaul@chromium.org BUG=b:141971239 TEST=boot Meep, run login_LoginSuccess Signed-off-by: Chiou, Cooper <cooper.chiou@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 07e17a75922a593393b7eb8f73622723b76d3706) Change-Id: I56a1c7781448abeb905107445df521a042dad64c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1857842 Tested-by: Cooper Chiou <cooper.chiou@intel.com> Tested-by: Henry Sun <henrysun@google.com> Commit-Ready: Marco Chen <marcochen@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Henry Sun <henrysun@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: drm/i915: Implement HDCP for DisplayPort This patch adds HDCP support for DisplayPort connectors by implementing the intel_hdcp_shim. Most of this is straightforward read/write from/to DPCD registers. One thing worth pointing out is the Aksv output bit. It wasn't easily separable like it's HDMI counterpart, so it's crammed in with the rest of it. Changes in v2: - Moved intel_hdcp_check_link out of intel_dp_check_link and only call it on short pulse. Since intel_hdcp_check_link does its own locking, this ensures we don't deadlock when intel_dp_check_link is called holding connection_mutex. - Rebased on drm-intel-next Changes in v3: - Initialize new worker Changes in v4: - Use intel_hdcp_init (Daniel) - Check for reauth requests in check_link (Ram) Changes in v5: - None Changes in v6: - Fix build warnings when printing ssize_t Cc: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Reviewed-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180108195545.218615-10-seanpaul@chromium.org Conflicts: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_dp.c intel_dp_hpd_pulse content fix BUG=b:141971239 TEST=boot Meep, run login_LoginSuccess, connect DP monitor Signed-off-by: Chiou, Cooper <cooper.chiou@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 20f24d776d1be6ecf353f21a158e7b716143e523) Change-Id: I3754bd48937ffaa72e9cade251a659ca582a5845 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1864892 Tested-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Marco Chen <marcochen@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org>

factory: dict.keys() in py2 change to list(dict) In python2, dict.keys() return a copy list of keys. In python3, dict.keys() return an iterator of keys. The semantic changes, so we need to use list(dict) to get a copy list. cheets_CTS/GTS: simplify the command generation logics Previously the command generation logics are devided into for-cts-instant and for-non-instant. This is because the CTS Instant doesn't support --include-filter option. This CL changes the rule to unify the logics: - For the test with one module: use --moduel option - For the test with multiple modules: use --include-filter option This rule is ok since the CTS instant only has the tests with one module. And this CL also changes the controlfiles accordingly.
